text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000096's 99215 excess sits mainly in moderately complex patients rather than low-complexity ones, but the few charts returned are too thin to tell upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 rate is not driven by low-complexity visits. At 0–1 conditions this provider tracks peers, and most of the excess falls on patients with 2–3 conditions, where the 99215 share runs well above the all-provider rate. That pattern could reflect a genuinely sicker panel or level inflation in the middle of the complexity range. The documentation leans in different directions. All three documented 99215s (C0053635, C0054199, C0054442) support high MDM, and the data-reviewed notes all have test lines on the claim. However, 3 of 7 documented 99214s came back at low MDM (e.g., C0053625, C0054102, C0054446), well above the comparison rate. With only 15 charts, that is a weak but notable signal, especially given how heavily this provider bills 99214. A reviewer should first request more charts, prioritizing 99214s and 99215s on 2–3 condition patients, along with low-acuity 99215s such as C0054144 (acute URI, no chronic conditions) and C0054435 (UTI in an 18-year-old)."}
